meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards are archived outside the ranking. Problems first resolved on or after 1 January 2026 can remain eligible, with dated evidence, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Subjective editorial preference requested by the user, based on saved titles and statement excerpts, with expanded summaries for sparse drafts. Scientific interest, breadth, conceptual clarity and topic diversity guide the explicit choices in research/editorial-ranking-20261023/decisions.json. This is not a new literature, formulation or current-open-status review. Formalization effort, prose length and publication date do not affect scores. Scores and focus prefixes were reconsidered. Equal scores express comparable preference; stable IDs break ties outside the focus prefix.

shared_definitions.scope: Shared terminology for the green selection reviewed on 20 November 2026. Each card specifies its input representation, parameters and cost model.

entries.title: How to read the shared definitions
entries.text:
Write \(N=|\langle X\rangle|\) for the length in bits of an encoded instance \(X\). On a SAT card, \(n\) usually counts variables. On a graph card, \(n\) usually counts vertices. Read the local definition before substituting either quantity into a bound. A truth table on \(n\) variables, for example, occupies \(2^n\) bits before a threshold or header is added.

For a Boolean function \(f\), \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathcal B}(f)\) denotes its minimum circuit size under the named basis and cost convention. A given circuit \(C\) has size \(s=|C|\). For a language \(L\), \(L_n\) is its characteristic function on \(n\)-bit strings. De Morgan formula leaf size is \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\).

A card's local definitions specify its model, promises and exceptions. The linked entries supply shared terminology, also available in the JSON exports.

entries.title: Input encodings and size parameters
entries.text:
For a finitely encoded object \(X\), write \(\langle X\rangle\) for its binary description and \(N=|\langle X\rangle|\) for its complete bit length. Count signs, indices, delimiters, coefficients and all explicitly supplied lists. An explicit table or syntax tree is supplied in full; a circuit or oracle generating it is a different representation. The card specifies the representation and the treatment of malformed inputs or inputs outside a promise.

Unless a card states otherwise, integer data in a bit model are binary, and rational data are signed binary numerators and positive binary denominators. Unary input is an explicit exception, as for some security parameters. The magnitude of an integer is not its bit length. An algorithm polynomial in numerical magnitude may take exponential time in a binary description.

Polynomial-time decidability is invariant under encodings interconvertible in polynomial time with polynomial output length. This does not preserve a precise exponent, a linear or quasilinear bound, or a circuit-size threshold. For those targets, retain the specific encoding and account for conversion costs. Bounds in a structural parameter must also account for the full supplied input; they are not promises of that running time for arbitrarily padded descriptions. An oracle, streaming, query or exact-real model has its own explicitly stated input-access costs.

entries.title: Asymptotic bounds and quantifiers
entries.text:
All unspecified logarithms have base two. \(f(n)=O(g(n))\) means that some constant \(C>0\) bounds \(f(n)\le Cg(n)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\); \(f=o(g)\) means \(f(n)/g(n)\to0\) where the ratio is defined. A polynomial bound has a fixed exponent and coefficient. Constants may depend on parameters declared fixed by the card, but not on varying instances.

Failure of a polynomial upper bound means that every proposed polynomial is exceeded at arbitrarily large lengths. It does not automatically mean a superpolynomial lower bound at every sufficiently large length. Preserve the displayed quantifier order. Likewise, a single \(2^{o(n)}\)-time algorithm and a separate \(2^{\varepsilon n}\)-time algorithm for each \(\varepsilon>0\) are not interchangeable without further conditions.

\(\operatorname{poly}(N)\) denotes some fixed polynomial factor. In SAT bounds such as \(2^{o(n)}\operatorname{poly}(N)\), \(n\) counts variables and \(N\) counts encoding bits. The meaning of \(\widetilde O\) and the parameters inside its suppressed logarithmic factors must follow the individual card.

entries.title: Uniform computation and bit cost
entries.text:
In the bit model, a uniform deterministic algorithm is one finite Turing-machine program for all input lengths, using a fixed number of tapes and finite tape alphabets. Each transition costs one step. Input access, integer arithmetic, auxiliary computation and writing output count. Polynomial time means a bound \(C(N+1)^k\) on every input of length \(N\), for fixed \(C,k\). The program receives no length-dependent advice or oracle unless the card explicitly supplies one.

A nondeterministic machine accepts when at least one branch accepts. A nondeterministic time bound applies to every branch. A randomized time guarantee and an expected-time guarantee are distinguished in the randomization entry. Polynomial-time class comparisons are robust under the usual polynomial-overhead machine simulations; precise time bounds must retain the machine model selected by the card.

entries.title: Languages, P, NP and coNP
entries.text:
A language is a set \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\). Membership is a total yes/no question, including the empty string. Its characteristic function at length \(n\) is \(L_n(x)=1\) exactly when \(x\in L\).

\(\mathrm{P}\) is the class of languages decided by uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithms in the bit model. A language is in \(\mathrm{NP}\) if there are a polynomial \(p\) and one deterministic polynomial-time verifier \(V\) such that
\[x\in L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in\{0,1\}^{\le p(|x|)}:\ V(x,y)=1.\]
The verifier halts on every pair, with time polynomial in \(|x|+|y|\); it accepts no allowed witness on a no-instance. The program and bounds are fixed independently of \(x\). This is equivalent to nondeterministic polynomial time. A language belongs to \(\mathrm{coNP}\) exactly when its complement in \(\{0,1\}^*\) belongs to \(\mathrm{NP}\). These are language classes; witness-output and promise problems require their own definitions.

entries.title: Decision and search reductions
entries.text:
A polynomial-time many-one (Karp) reduction from \(A\) to \(B\) is one total uniform deterministic polynomial-time function \(f\) satisfying \(x\in A\iff f(x)\in B\). It writes one entire target instance. A language is NP-hard under these reductions when every NP language reduces to it, and NP-complete when it is also in NP. Other completeness notions must name their reduction type.

For search relations \(R,Q\), a polynomial-time many-one search reduction consists of two polynomial-time maps \(F,G\). The output instance must belong to the target domain for every input in the source domain. For every such input \(x\) and every valid answer \(z\) to \(Q\) on \(F(x)\), one requires \(R(x,G(x,z))\). Time is measured in \(|x|\) for \(F\) and \(|x|+|z|\) for \(G\). Correctness must hold for every accepted target answer. Domain and malformed-input conventions remain local.

A Turing reduction may instead make adaptive oracle queries. Logarithmic-space, randomized, promise-preserving and count-preserving reductions are separate notions. Do not replace one by another when normalizing wording.

entries.title: SAT, CNF-SAT, k-SAT and Circuit-SAT
entries.text:
SAT asks whether an explicitly encoded Boolean formula has a satisfying assignment. A formula is a finite tree over variables, constants 0 and 1, binary AND and OR, and unary NOT. Repeated subexpressions are written separately. A literal is a variable or its negation. A CNF formula is a conjunction of clauses, each a disjunction of literals. In this glossary, \(k\)-CNF means at most \(k\) literals per clause; an exactly-\(k\) convention must be stated locally. An empty conjunction is true and an empty clause is false.

\(n\) counts variables, \(m\) counts clauses when applicable, and \(N\) is the full encoding length. Binary variable indices and delimiters contribute to \(N\). SAT, CNF-SAT and 3-SAT are polynomial-time interreducible, but a reduction may change the number of variables and the precise running-time bound. A card's restricted syntax, numbering and padding rules remain part of its problem.

Circuit-SAT receives a circuit DAG, which can share subcomputations. This is not a formula tree. MCSP instead receives a full truth table of length \(2^n\), together with its size threshold. A clause-incidence encoding of 3-SAT is another explicitly identified representation. Never identify these input lengths.

entries.title: Boolean circuits and minimum circuit size
entries.text:
A Boolean circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with designated input wires and one or more ordered outputs. Gate values can be reused; fan-out and depth are unrestricted unless restricted locally. Correctness is exact on the card's entire domain, or on its stated promise set. Circuits for different lengths are nonuniform unless a uniform constructor is explicitly required.

In the \(\mathrm{DM}\) convention, gates are binary AND and OR and unary NOT. All operation gates, including NOT, cost one; input wires, constant sources 0 and 1, wires and output designations are free. An output may be an input, a constant or a gate. In the \(B_2\) convention, any Boolean function of at most two input bits is a unit-cost gate, with the same free sources and wires. Write \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\) or \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(f)\) for the minimum gate count. Multiple outputs share one joint budget.

The subscript \(\mathcal B\) in \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathcal B}\) records the basis and cost convention. In the \(\mathrm{DM+c}\) convention, constants are gates of cost one and the other De Morgan costs are the same. For a language, apply it to \(L_n\), not to the infinite language without specifying a length. \(s=|C|\) denotes the size of a given circuit, not a minimum. Fixed complete bounded-fan-in bases preserve polynomial size and linear-size existence up to constant factors; they do not preserve exact optimum sizes or exact MCSP thresholds.

A threshold-circuit card specifies how a majority gate treats an even tie and whether size charges wires. Each occurrence of a repeated input counts separately when wires are charged. Modular gates and unbounded fan-in also require a named basis. Use the card's cost convention when comparing exact size thresholds.

entries.title: De Morgan formulas and leaf size
entries.text:
A De Morgan formula is a rooted tree with binary AND/OR and unary NOT operations, variable leaves and optional constants. Internal computations cannot be shared. The size convention \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\) is the minimum number of variable-leaf occurrences in a formula computing \(f\) exactly. Positive and negative occurrences each count, including repeated occurrences of the same variable. Constant leaves are free. Constants have size zero and a literal has size one. Pushing negations to the leaves preserves this measure.

Formula leaf size, circuit gate count and circuit depth are distinct measures. A source may call formula size \(L(f)\) and circuit size \(S(f)\); revised cards use \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\) and \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\) while retaining original symbols in source quotations. Restricted, arithmetic or other formula models must retain their own cost conventions.

entries.title: L, NL and PSPACE
entries.text:
Space is the number of work-tape cells visited, with fixed finite alphabets; the read-only input is not charged. The classes \(\mathrm{L}\) and \(\mathrm{NL}\) use deterministic and nondeterministic machines, respectively, with \(O(\log(N+2))\) workspace. Nondeterministic acceptance is existential over branches; a polynomial clock can be imposed for NL. A halting deterministic logspace machine has only polynomially many configurations and therefore polynomial running time.

\(\mathrm{PSPACE}\) consists of languages decided by halting deterministic machines with polynomial workspace. It imposes no polynomial time bound. Read-only input, output-tape access, catalytic storage and other auxiliary memory conventions must not be changed when a card specifies a different space model.

entries.title: EXP, NEXP and their complements
entries.text:
\(\mathrm{EXP}\), also called \(\mathrm{EXPTIME}\), is deterministic time \(2^{N^{O(1)}}\), the union over fixed polynomial exponents. \(\mathrm{NEXP}\) is the corresponding nondeterministic class, with every branch time-bounded. Equivalent bounds can be written \(C2^{(N+1)^k}\) for fixed positive integers \(C,k\). \(\mathrm{coNEXP}\) consists of complements of NEXP languages. Machines are uniform and have no advice unless a suffix explicitly supplies it.

\(\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{O(N)})\) and \(\mathrm{NE}=\mathrm{NTIME}(2^{O(N)})\) have linear exponents. They are distinct definitions from EXP and NEXP; any use of padding to relate particular containment questions must be justified locally.

entries.title: BPP, RP and randomized guarantees
entries.text:
\(\mathrm{BPP}\) consists of languages decided by one uniform randomized Turing machine in polynomial time on every input and every random tape, with error at most \(1/3\) on each individual input. Random bits are independent and unbiased. \(\mathrm{RP}\) has the same worst-case time convention, never accepts a no-instance, and accepts each yes-instance with probability at least \(1/2\). Constant error thresholds can be amplified within polynomial time.

A Las Vegas algorithm is always correct whenever it outputs and terminates with probability one; a claimed expected-time bound averages over its internal randomness for each fixed input. This differs from a worst-case bound on every random tape. A Monte Carlo guarantee permits a stated error probability. Average-case input distributions, simultaneous correctness over a sequence of queries, and adaptive adversaries are specified locally. Do not turn any of these into a blanket BPP guarantee.

entries.title: Nonuniformity, P/poly and advice
entries.text:
\(\mathrm{P/poly}\) consists of languages whose functions \(L_n\) have Boolean circuits of size at most \(C(n+1)^k\), for constants depending on the language. One circuit is chosen for each length; no computable circuit generator is required. This is equivalent to deterministic polynomial time with a polynomial-length advice string \(a_n\) depending only on the input length.

More generally, a suffix /poly supplies polynomial-length advice that is fixed before the instance is chosen. Advice need not be computable. For NEXP/poly, the nondeterministic running time is exponential in a polynomial of the original input length. The familiar equality of some advised classes does not establish the equality of their uniform versions. Any circuit uniformity condition, oracle, shared randomness or input-dependent information is a separate model choice.

entries.title: FP, #P and total NP search
entries.text:
FP denotes total functions computed by deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines, with output bits charged. A nonnegative integer output is written in binary unless stated otherwise. A #P function has the form
\[f(x)=|\{y\in\{0,1\}^{p(|x|)}:V(x,y)=1\}|,\]
where \(p\) is a polynomial and \(V\) a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. Count distinct witness strings, even if several represent the same object. Padding must preserve these counts; ordinary existence-preserving NP reductions need not do so.

TFNP concerns polynomially balanced, polynomial-time decidable relations \(R(x,y)\) with at least one valid answer for every input. A polynomial-time algorithm for a search relation selects some valid answer. This relation-solving usage of FP is explicitly identified on search cards. Search, decision and exact counting are different tasks.

entries.title: Word RAM, real RAM and oracle access
entries.text:
A word RAM stores words of the bit width stated by the card, usually \(\Theta(\log(n+2))\). Each card lists its finite set of unit-cost instructions or explicitly selects the integer instructions below. The availability of multiplication, division, random words, packed input and precomputed tables is not inferred from the name alone. Multiword arithmetic is charged by its component operations. A polynomial-time equivalence with Turing machines does not justify transferring a precise exponent without overhead.

Integer instructions for cards that explicitly select them. On unsigned \(w\)-bit words, allow addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), integer quotient and remainder by a nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, logical shifts, comparison, copying, branching, and random-access reads and writes. Each costs one step. A shift by at least \(w\) gives zero. Multiword operations cost their component steps. A memory instruction accesses one word. Random bits or words, and the cost of generating them, are specified by the individual card.

A real RAM or algebraic model may charge exact operations on reals at unit cost. It is not a bit-cost algorithm on arbitrary precision rational data. Query and oracle models charge the specified accesses and may deliberately leave the oracle's internal computation uncharged. Streaming passes, online deadlines and data-structure preprocessing and queries keep their local costs.

entries.title: Arithmetic circuits and field conventions
entries.text:
An arithmetic circuit is a DAG computing a polynomial through arithmetic operations over the specified field or ring. Unless a card explicitly uses a different notion, polynomial equality means equality as formal polynomials, not agreement only on selected evaluation points. The field, permitted constants, division gates, commutativity and size measure are part of the model.

Boolean \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathcal B}\) does not stand for arithmetic circuit complexity. Arithmetic cards keep a field-qualified local notation and explicitly say whether they count input gates, operation gates, wires, or some combination. Arbitrary field constants of unit cost do not have the same meaning as finitely encoded binary constants. Changing among these conventions can preserve some asymptotic questions but requires checking the target; no global change of field, constants or uniformity is made here.

entries.title: Security parameters and negligible functions
entries.text:
The security parameter is \(\lambda\) when not locally rebound, and unary \(1^\lambda\) input is used when the card specifies it. Polynomial security bounds are in \(\lambda\), not in the bit length of a binary spelling of \(\lambda\). A nonnegative function \(\nu\) is negligible if, for every constant \(c>0\), \(\nu(\lambda)<\lambda^{-c}\) for all sufficiently large \(\lambda\).

The adversary's uniformity, advice, auxiliary input, oracle access, interaction and probability space are specified by the security experiment. A polynomial-size circuit adversary is not the same model as a uniform probabilistic polynomial-time machine. Information-theoretic, statistical and computational guarantees must retain their quantifiers and error parameters.

entries.title: Graphs and structural size
entries.text:
Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \([0]=\varnothing\). For a finite graph \(G=(V,E)\), \(n=|V|\) and \(m=|E|\) are structural counts, not automatically its bit length. The card specifies whether edges are directed, loops or parallel edges are allowed, and whether labels, weights and a distinguished vertex form part of the input.

Adjacency matrices, adjacency lists and edge lists are different encodings. Binary endpoints typically cost logarithmically many bits, and binary weights contribute their full bit lengths. Query access to adjacency is another model. Graphs used as mathematical objects in an existence question need not be algorithmic inputs at all. No global simplicity, connectivity or representation assumption is imposed by a link to this entry.

entries.title: The polynomial hierarchy and TQBF
entries.text:
Set \(\Sigma_0^{\mathrm P}=\Pi_0^{\mathrm P}=\mathrm P\). For fixed \(k\ge1\), membership in \(L\in\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\) is expressed by a uniform deterministic polynomial-time predicate \(R\) and a polynomial \(p\). For each input \(x\), choose \(k\) strings of length \(p(|x|)\) under alternating quantifiers, starting with an existential quantifier. Then \(x\in L\) exactly when the resulting quantified predicate \(R(x,y_1,\ldots,y_k)\) is true. A block quantifies an entire string. \(\Pi_k^{\mathrm P}\) consists of the complements of these languages, and \(\mathrm{PH}=\bigcup_{k\ge0}\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\). The level, polynomial and predicate are fixed for the language.

TQBF is the language of true, fully quantified Boolean formulas. Every variable in the Boolean matrix is bound by the prefix, each quantifier ranges over one bit, and malformed encodings are rejected. The number of blocks in an input can grow with its length. TQBF is PSPACE-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.

entries.title: Parameterized time and reductions
entries.text:
A parameterized instance has a finite description and a distinguished nonnegative integer \(k\). Let \(N\) be the complete encoded length. A fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) decision algorithm runs in \(f(k)(N+1)^c\) steps for a total computable \(f\) and one constant \(c\) independent of \(k\). The card fixes how the parameter is encoded. A polynomial exponent that may depend on \(k\) gives a different guarantee.

An FPT many-one reduction computes an equivalent target instance \((x',k')\) within such a time bound and guarantees \(k'\le g(k)\) for a total computable \(g\). Kernelization additionally uses polynomial preprocessing time and bounds the size of the resulting instance as a function of \(k\).

entries.title: Finite words and finite automata
entries.text:
An alphabet \(\Sigma\) is a finite set of symbols. The set \(\Sigma^*\) contains all finite words, including the empty word \(\varepsilon\). Word length counts symbols. A complete one-way deterministic finite automaton has a finite state set \(Q\) and transition function \(\delta:Q\times\Sigma\to Q\). Its extension to words starts at the given state and reads symbols from left to right. Acceptance uses an initial state and a set of final states when the task calls for a language.

A nondeterministic automaton can have several transitions. A word is accepted if it has an accepting run. Unambiguity permits at most one accepting run per word. Two-way heads, endmarkers, empty moves, and acceptance of infinite words use the conventions on the individual card.

entries.title: Approximation ratios and rounding
entries.text:
For a minimization problem with nonnegative costs, a factor \(\alpha\ge1\) bounds the cost of a feasible output by \(\alpha\,\operatorname{OPT}\). For a nonnegative maximization problem a card may use a fraction \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and require value at least \(\rho\,\operatorname{OPT}\). The inequality also specifies the guarantee when the optimum is zero. An additive error has the units of the objective.

For a randomized algorithm, read whether the inequality holds in expectation or with a specified probability on each instance. Expected cost and expected running time concern different random quantities. For a minimization relaxation with a positive lower bound, its integrality gap is the supremum of the integral-to-relaxed optimum ratio over the stated instances. An algorithmic target also counts the cost of finding a feasible solution.

entries.title: Total variation and mixing time
entries.text:
The total variation distance between probability laws \(\mu,
u\) on the same measurable space is \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu,
u)=\sup_A|\mu(A)-
u(A)|\), where \(A\) ranges over measurable events. On a finite state space \(\Omega\) it equals \(	frac12\sum_{x\in\Omega}|\mu(x)-
u(x)|\).

For a discrete-time Markov chain with transition matrix \(P\) and stationary law \(\pi\), the worst-start mixing time at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is the least \(t\ge0\) with \(\max_x d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P^t(x,\cdot),\pi)\le\varepsilon\), or infinity if there is no such time. A transition, a whole sweep and one unit of continuous time have different costs. The card fixes the clock, starting law and tolerance.

entries.title: Online cost and competitive ratio
entries.text:
An online rule sees requests in arrival order. At time \(t\) it may use the observed prefix and its allowed internal state. The offline optimum knows the full sequence and obeys the resource and feasibility constraints specified for it. For a minimization problem, a typical competitive bound is \(\operatorname{cost}_A(\sigma)\le r\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma)+b\). The card says whether an additive constant is allowed and what it may depend on.

For a randomized rule and an oblivious adversary, the request sequence is fixed independently of the random bits. Expected cost is then taken for each such sequence. Random-order input, adaptive adversaries and regret against a fixed comparator define different guarantees.

entries.title: Streaming passes and memory
entries.text:
A stream supplies a sequence of records. A pass is one traversal in the stated order. In a one-pass algorithm, later computation can use an earlier record only through information saved when it was available. Space counts bits or words according to the card, including any retained seeds or buffers that its model charges.

An insertion-only stream, a stream with deletions and a uniformly random permutation of a fixed multiset give different inputs. Read the local convention for order, precision, success probability, permitted preprocessing and the size of the output.

entries.title: The cell-probe model
entries.text:
A data structure stores information in cells of \(w\) bits. A query may choose its next address using the query and values returned by earlier probes. Reading or writing a cell counts as a probe under the local rules. Computation between probes is free. Space counts available cells, or their bits if specified.

The card sets \(w\), the allowed preprocessing, private state, and any randomness. In a static problem the stored data do not change between queries. A dynamic problem specifies updates and whether the bound applies to each operation or is amortized over a sequence.

entries.title: Learning error, examples and confidence
entries.text:
For a classifier \(h\) and a joint law \(D\) of labeled examples, its zero-one error is \(\Pr_{(X,Y)\sim D}[h(X)\ne Y]\). In a realizable problem, the target class contains a hypothesis with zero error. An agnostic excess-error guarantee compares the output with the infimum of the error over the reference class. A proper learner must return a member of that class.

The confidence statement concerns the training sample and the learner's own randomness. The output's prediction error concerns a fresh draw from the specified distribution. The card fixes the sampling or query access, distribution family, loss, and whether time includes evaluating the returned hypothesis.

entries.title: Uniform quantum computation and BQP
entries.text:
A BQP computation decides a language using a uniform polynomial-size family of quantum circuits over a fixed efficiently specified universal gate set, with acceptance probability at least \(2/3\) on yes-inputs and at most \(1/3\) on no-inputs. Repetition with fresh work registers can reduce the error. The uniform constructor and input encoding are part of the model.

A quantum query counts an invocation of the specified oracle. A channel capacity, a quantum proof system and the distinguishing power of a restricted gate set each require their own resource and success definitions.

entries.title: Unit-cost string edit distance
entries.text:
For finite strings \(x,y\), their unit-cost edit distance is the smallest number of single-symbol insertions, deletions and substitutions that transform \(x\) into \(y\). Identical symbols may be matched at zero cost. Length counts symbols. The alphabet, representation, and the resource used to read each symbol are given locally.

An approximation to this distance, an edit script, and aligning more than two strings are different outputs. Tree edits and insertion/deletion-only metrics have their own local operations.

entries.title: Finite relational structures and conjunctive queries
entries.text:
A finite relational signature lists relation symbols and their arities. A structure interprets an \(r\)-ary symbol as a set of ordered \(r\)-tuples on its domain. A homomorphism maps elements of one structure into the other so that every tuple present in a relation maps to a tuple in the same relation. A conjunctive query existentially quantifies a conjunction of relational atoms, leaving any answer variables free.

Under set semantics a tuple is either present or absent. Under bag semantics occurrences carry multiplicity. Data complexity fixes the schema and query and varies the database. Combined complexity can include the query as input. The card specifies which objects vary, its access model and the semantics of constraints, answers or repairs.

entries.title: The SAT encoding for ETH and SETH
entries.text:
For a nonnegative integer \(a\), let \(b\) be the length of the binary expansion of \(a+1\). Define \(\operatorname{code}(a)=1^b0\,\operatorname{bin}(a+1)\). Codes are self-delimiting. With a fixed width bound \(q\ge3\), encode a CNF by \(\operatorname{code}(n)\), \(\operatorname{code}(m)\), then the \(m\) clauses in list order. A clause begins with its coded literal count. Each literal has a sign bit (zero for positive) and a coded index from \(1\) through \(n\). Every declared variable must occur. A clause may contain up to \(q\) literals, including zero. Repetitions and both signs of a variable are allowed. All lists must be complete and consume the entire input.

For a valid formula \(F\), \(n(F)\) counts its distinct variables and \(N(F)\) counts every encoded bit. On every valid formula, the uniform deterministic multitape machine must halt and decide satisfiability exactly. On malformed strings it must reject in time polynomial in their bit length. The running-time bound on valid formulas is the one in the display below. At each fixed \(q\), define \(s_q\) as the infimum of the \(\alpha\ge0\) for which some such machine and constants \(C\ge1\), \(d\in\mathbb N_0\) satisfy
\[t_A(F)\le C\,2^{\alpha n(F)}(N(F)+1)^d\]
on every valid input. Testing all assignments shows \(0\le s_q\le1\). The machine and constants may depend on \(q,\alpha\). ETH concerns \(s_3\) and SETH concerns the limiting behavior as \(q\) grows.

entries.title: Certified numerical answers and infimum exponents
entries.text:
When a card asks for a numerical value \(x\) to absolute error \(\delta\), an answer \(a\) must come with a proof of \(|a-x|\le\delta\). One way is to prove \(\ell\le x\le u\) with \(u-\ell\le2\delta\), then take \(a=(\ell+u)/2\). The answer must specify its value independently of the optimization, limit or unknown quantity the card asks to determine. For a function on a domain \(D\), supply one description of a function \(g\) and prove \(|g(t)-x(t)|\le\delta\) for every \(t\in D\). Two described bounding functions of pointwise width at most \(2\delta\) give such a \(g\) by their midpoint. An exact expression also qualifies. Each card specifies its own precision, any restriction on answer values, and its proof requirements. An interval may enclose an infimum or supremum even when no feasible object attains it.

For a growth exponent defined by \(x=\inf\{a:f(n)=O(n^a)\}\), the implicit constant and the threshold must obey the card’s uniformity requirements. The definition alone supplies neither an \(O(n^x)\) bound at the endpoint nor a limit for \(\log f(n)/\log n\).

entries.title: Synchronous LOCAL and CONGEST rounds
entries.text:
The communication network is a graph. Nodes run a distributed algorithm in synchronous rounds, exchanging messages with their neighbors. LOCAL permits arbitrarily long finite messages. CONGEST bounds the number of bits sent along each edge in each direction per round, typically by \(O(\log n)\) for \(n\) nodes. Local computation is unrestricted between rounds when the card specifies that convention.

The initial information, identifiers, shared or private randomness, and per-node outputs belong to the particular problem. A high-probability guarantee can concern one node or simultaneous correctness of all outputs. The statement specifies which event and which randomness the probability concerns.
